To address this issue, Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods have been introduced, enabling adaptation with a reduced number of trainable parameters. Among these techniques, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has gained widespread recognition for its efficiency and ease of integration. This survey provides a thorough exploration of LoRA, covering its mathematical principles, implementation techniques, and real-world applications. By comparing LoRA to traditional full fine-tuning and other PEFT methods, we highlight its ability to maintain strong performance while significantly cutting down on computational overhead. Empirical evaluations across various NLP benchmarks further demonstrate its effectiveness in reducing memory consumption without sacrificing accuracy. Beyond its advantages, we also examine the challenges associated with LoRA, such as rank selection sensitivity, compatibility with different model architectures, and potential hardware optimizations. Additionally, we discuss promising future directions, including hybrid fine-tuning strategies, dynamic rank adjustment, and expansion into multi-modal learning. By enabling more efficient adaptation of complex models, LoRA represents a crucial advancement in scalable fine-tuning. This survey aims to serve as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners looking to leverage LoRA for optimized model training across diverse requires accurate domain understanding, clause retrieval, and evidence-grounded generation, yet general-purpose large language models often lack sufficient domain adaptation and factual support. This study proposes a textile-standard question-answering framework that integrates Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning with multidimensional retrieval-augmented generation (MDRAG). Based on 7017 domestic and international textile standards, we constructed a structured knowledge resource containing 121,166 annotated domain elements and a task-specific dataset of 2000 question\u2013answer pairs. Qwen3.5-9B-Base, Llama 3.1-8B-Instruct, and GLM-4-9B were evaluated under three primary settings: Baseline, Baseline+LoRA, and Baseline+LoRA+MDRAG. A separate comparison with conventional RAG was conducted to assess the additional benefit of multidimensional retrieval over single-path retrieval. Among the primary settings, Qwen3.5-9B-Base with LoRA+MDRAG achieved the highest overall performance, with a cosine similarity of 0.624, a BLEU score of 0.283, and an expert-based overall score of 24.4. These findings support the use of lightweight domain adaptation together with multidimensional structured knowledge retrieval for textile-standard question
